newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEONARD CHARGES INTO LEAD AT WESTERN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD CHARGES INTO LEAD AT WESTERN OPEN.

text.p: Justin Leonard carded an eight-under-par 64, the day's lowest round by three strokes, to charge into a two-stroke lead after the second round of the $2 million Western Open on Friday.
Leonard, who won the Kemper Open four weeks ago, reeled off nine birdies and one bogey on an unseasonally cool afternoon at the Cog Hill course on the outskirts of Chicago.
He posted a nine-under 135 halfway total to lead by two strokes from fellow-Americans Billy Andrade (67), Mike Hulbert (68) and Michael Bradley (68).
First-round leader Mark O'Meara (73) bogeyed the first three holes but recovered to remain in the hunt, four strokes from the lead in a group that included Tiger Woods (72).

Leonard, one of the most consistent players on the U.S. PGA Tour this year, was on fire on the greens on a day when the field averaged 72.6 strokes, more than a stroke lower than in the windswept first round.
"I read the putts well and hit good putts where I meant to," Leonard said.

However, he was not as happy with his accuracy off the tee with the new titanium-headed driver that he switched to in May after discarding his trusty old wood, long after most other players had done so.
"I didn't drive the ball that great today," he continued. "I didn't hit a fairway until (number) seven."
Nonetheless, Leonard said he is happy with his new driver, which he says has added more than 10 yards in length to his tee shots.
"It's taken some of the pressure off the other parts of my game. It's a lot of fun. I'm able to play more aggressively."
Woods also drove the ball inaccurately, hitting just seven fairways. He mixed three birdies with three bogeys, and clearly was unhappy with his performance.
"It was a frustrating round. I didn't seem to have the same intensity level," he lamented. "I left a lot of shots out there, but I am still in the tournament."
Eighty players made the cut, which fell at two-over 146.
